items.detail: The **S&P 500** fell **2.68%** to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq lost 3.37% to 24,579.42, despite a Friday bounce in AI shares.
items.why: After Democrats swept Congress, investors feared tighter AI and data-center rules and dumped tech.

items.detail: On Thursday the Nasdaq fell **5.5%**, its worst day since 2020, while chip stocks lost more than 12% and Nvidia about 9%.
items.why: Worries about regulation hit the most crowded AI trades hardest, including memory makers and data-center names.

items.detail: Friday's jobs report showed **165,000** new jobs in October, far above forecasts, and markets now see a December Fed rate hike as likely.
items.why: Strong hiring and wage growth of 0.4% suggest the economy can handle higher rates.

items.detail: Asian tech markets took the brunt of the global AI selloff. Taiwan had its **worst week since 2001** and entered a bear market, and Korea's KOSPI hit a circuit breaker.
items.why: Fears of US limits on AI spending hit chipmakers, which make up a big share of both markets.

items.detail: The **NIFTY 50** jumped **8.6%** to 25,030, its best week in about six years, with banks leading a seven-session winning streak.
items.why: Foreign investors bought nearly $3 billion of Indian stocks as a sharp fall in oil helped the oil-importing economy.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** fell about **2.1%** to around 2,754, after a 4.4% drop on Thursday and a partial rebound on Friday.
items.why: The AI selloff spread to small caps, and higher odds of a rate hike mean tighter borrowing costs for small firms.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** rose above $80,000 after the midterms, then fell back to about **$75,500**, heading for a fifth straight weekly loss of roughly 3%.
items.why: Traders fear tougher crypto rules from a Democratic Congress, and the strong jobs report raised the odds of a rate hike.

items.detail: **Ether** slipped about **2%** on the week to roughly $2,250 and fell below its 200-day average.
items.why: Spot ether ETFs kept losing money, about $657 million over the week.

items.detail: **Solana** dropped below $100 to about **$89.65**, its sixth straight weekly decline, and is testing a long-term trendline.
items.why: The selloff across risky assets after the midterms hit the more volatile coins hardest, and money flowed out of Solana ETFs.

items.detail: **Spot gold** rose about **5%** on the week to near $4,077, its best week in over two months, recovering from last week's one-year low.
items.why: Hopes of US-Iran de-escalation pushed oil down, which eased inflation worries and weakened the dollar and bond yields.

crossCuttingTheme: The Democrats' midterm sweep pulled markets two ways: fears of AI regulation sank tech stocks in the US, Korea and Taiwan and dragged down crypto, while hopes of US-Iran de-escalation cut oil prices, lifting gold and oil-importing India.
